issues.legal_issue: Retrospective validation of a marriage invalid only because the spouses belonged to different castes or communities makes a child of that marriage legitimate and entitled to coparcenary rights.
material_facts: A child brought a partition suit claiming a share in the joint family property as a member of the father's coparcenary.
The courts below found that the parents had married and that the child was born of that marriage.
The marriage took place before the applicable law retrospectively validated marriages invalid only because the spouses belonged to different castes or communities.
The child claimed rights in the father's joint family property.
issues.conclusion: The marriage was valid, and the child was legitimate and entitled to the rights of a coparcener in the joint family property.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Hindu Marriages Validity Act, 1949, retrospectively validates marriages between Hindus that were invalid only because the parties belonged to different religions, castes, sub-castes or sects. The validity of the marriage necessarily makes its issue legitimate; the express reference to legitimacy in section 1 of the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856, was included as a matter of abundant caution, and its absence from the 1949 Act does not alter that consequence. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.partition_suit_claiming_coparcenary_righ: A child brought a partition proceeding and claimed rights in a parent's joint family property as a coparcener.
predicates.child_born_of_marriage: The child was born of the marriage whose validity is at issue.
predicates.marriage_predated_validation: The marriage occurred before the applicable law took effect.
predicates.applicable_law_retroactively_validates_m: The applicable law retrospectively validates marriages that were invalid only because the spouses belonged to different communities.

issues.definition: When a child born of a pre-existing marriage claims coparcenary rights in a partition proceeding and the applicable law retrospectively validates the marriage despite its community difference, the child is legitimate and entitled to those rights.

issues.legal_issue: Concurrent factual findings in an appeal are not reassessed when the appellant identifies no misreading of evidence or other error warranting reassessment.
material_facts: The courts below concurrently found that the parents had married and that the child was born of that marriage.
In the appeal, the appellant challenged those findings as based on misreading of evidence.
The appellant did not identify any such misreading or other error that would justify reassessing the evidence.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent findings concerning the marriage and the child's parentage were left undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to reassess concurrent factual findings where the appellant could point to no misreading of important evidence or other error justifying reassessment. No provision or earlier case was relied on for this point.

predicates.appeal_challenging_concurrent_factual_fi: An appellant challenged factual findings reached by both lower courts.
predicates.no_misreading_or_other_reassessment_erro: The appellant identified no misreading of evidence or other error that would justify reassessing the facts.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges concurrent factual findings but identifies no misreading or other reassessment error, those findings remain undisturbed.
